name: Castle and Nakamachi/Nawate Old Streets
tagline: Historic heart around the black castle
description: The atmospheric core around Matsumoto-jo, where preserved merchant houses line the Nakamachi and Nawate old streets. Craft shops, cafes, sake sellers, and storehouses give this walkable district a heritage charm that captures the city's traditional castle-town character beautifully.
bestFor: Culture lovers who want heritage streets, cafes, and the castle nearby
pros: Rich traditional atmosphere and craft shops
Highly walkable with the castle on your doorstep
cons: Busier with tourists in peak season

name: Matsumoto Station and City Centre
description: The bustling area around Matsumoto Station, the city's transport and commercial hub. Chain cafes, restaurants, shops, and hotels cluster here, with limited express trains linking Tokyo and Nagoya. It is the most convenient, well-serviced base for a nomad who values connectivity.
bestFor: Nomads wanting transport links, shops, and everyday convenience close at hand
pros: Plenty of shops, cafes, and restaurants
Easy day trips to the mountains
cons: Less charming than the old streets
Busier and noisier around the station

name: Asama Onsen Hot-Spring District
tagline: Relaxed hot-spring quarter northeast of centre
description: A traditional hot-spring district northeast of the centre, where ryokan and public baths draw on natural onsen waters. Quieter and more residential than downtown, it offers a restful, characterful base with a slower pace and easy bus links back into the city.
bestFor: Those wanting onsen relaxation and calm away from the busy centre
pros: Natural hot springs and ryokan atmosphere
cons: A bus ride from the centre

name: Shinshu University Area
description: The residential and student districts toward Shinshu University, southeast of the centre. Cheaper rents, casual eateries, and everyday shops give it a relaxed, lived-in feel. It suits budget-minded nomads happy to trade central charm for lower costs and a local, unhurried rhythm.
bestFor: Budget nomads and long-stayers wanting cheaper rent and everyday local life
cons: Further from castle and old streets
